topic: She seems to have left already
title: She seems to have left already
pt: Foco da aula: perfect infinitive: seem / appear + to have + particípio

solo90.name: Pausa

lines.en: Rui, do you know where the finance manager is? Her desk is empty, and her laptop isn’t here either.
lines.pt: Rui, você sabe onde está a gerente de finanças? A mesa dela está vazia e o notebook também não está aqui.

lines.en: She seems to have left already. Her coat is gone, and the cleaner said the lights were off when she came in.
lines.pt: Parece que ela já saiu. O casaco dela sumiu, e a faxineira disse que as luzes estavam apagadas quando chegou.

lines.en: But we have a meeting at nine, and she promised to bring the budget report. I need her to start.
lines.pt: Mas temos reunião às nove e ela prometeu trazer o relatório do orçamento. Preciso dela para começar.

lines.en: Maybe she was called to the other building. She appears to have forgotten the meeting, though, because her calendar says nothing.
lines.pt: Talvez a tenham chamado ao outro prédio. Mas ela parece ter esquecido a reunião, porque a agenda dela não diz nada.

lines.en: That doesn’t sound like her. She is usually the first one here, and she has never missed a deadline.
lines.pt: Não é a cara dela. Ela costuma ser a primeira a chegar e nunca perdeu um prazo.

lines.en: True, but the printer seems to have broken down again, so she may have gone downstairs to print everything.
lines.pt: Verdade, mas a impressora parece ter quebrado de novo, então ela pode ter descido para imprimir tudo.

lines.en: Could be. I’ll call her phone, and if she doesn’t answer, we will have to postpone the meeting until Thursday.
lines.pt: Pode ser. Vou ligar para ela e, se não atender, vamos ter que adiar a reunião para quinta.

lines.en: Wait, I hear someone in the corridor. It sounds like her, and she seems to have run all the way from the station.
lines.pt: Espera, ouvi alguém no corredor. Parece ela, e parece que correu desde a estação.

lines.en: Then she has a good excuse. Let’s give her a minute to breathe before we ask about the budget, all right?
lines.pt: Então ela tem uma boa desculpa. Vamos dar um minuto para ela respirar antes de perguntar do orçamento, certo?

lines.en: Agreed. She would have told us if she had planned to be late, so I think something unexpected happened on the way.
lines.pt: Combinado. Ela teria nos avisado se tivesse planejado atrasar, então acho que algo inesperado aconteceu no caminho.

lines.en: Fine. I’ll make her a cup of coffee, and you can open the meeting room and turn on the projector.
lines.pt: Certo. Vou fazer um café para ela e você abre a sala de reunião e liga o projetor.

facts.label: Dedução sobre o passado
facts.sub: Use seem ou appear com to have + particípio para dizer o que provavelmente já aconteceu: She seems to have left already.

facts.label: Infinitivo perfeito
facts.sub: Para deduzir algo que já aconteceu, use seem / appear + to have + particípio: She seems to have left. He appears to have forgotten. A ação veio antes do momento em que você fala.

facts.label: Evidências
facts.sub: Use a estrutura quando houver pistas: o casaco sumiu, a mesa está vazia, a agenda está em branco. Ela suaviza a frase, porque você tem uma impressão, não certeza total.

compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “parece que ela já saiu” e “ela parece ter esquecido”.
compare.us: Em inglês: She seems to have left. She appears to have forgotten. O infinitivo perfeito (to have + particípio) olha para o passado.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: She seems to have left means the leaving happened before now.
We say “She seems to has left”.
items.why: After to, the verb is have.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: She seems to have left means the leaving happened before now. → Verdadeiro (The perfect infinitive looks back.)
We say “She seems to has left”. → Falso (After to, the verb is have.)
Appear can replace seem here. → Verdadeiro (Both are common.)

pages.title: An empty desk · 1/3
paragraphs: It is eight fifty on a grey morning in Boston. The office is quiet. Dirk walks past the finance manager’s desk. Nothing is there. Rui looks at a calendar. They have ten minutes before the meeting.

“Rui, do you know where the finance manager is? Her desk is empty, and her laptop isn’t here either.” says Dirk. “She seems to have left already. Her coat is gone, and the cleaner said the lights were off when she came in.” says Rui. “But we have a meeting at nine, and she promised to bring the budget report. I need her to start.” says Dirk.
